root.name: Bird Opening: Siegener Gambit
root.moves: 1. f4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. Nf3 c5 4. c3

overview: In From's Gambit move order White plays 2.d4 exd4 3.Nf3 c5 4.c3, offering the d-pawn to open lines and develop quickly. Black takes with 4...dxc3 and accepts a sharp fight or keeps the pawn with ...Nc6. White aims for fast development with Nxc3 and Bc4 or Qb3 against f7 and the weakened diagonals. Unclear theory; reasoned from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on c3 with Nxc3, develop Bc4 and Qb3 against f7.
Use f4 and Nf3 to hit e5 and g7 with rapid development.

black_ideas.idea: Take cxd4 and hold the extra pawn with ...Nc6 and ...d6.

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black pawns on c5 and d4 and White pieces developing against them.

character.notes: White gives material for development and both kings can come under fire.

gambit.notes: White offers the d4 pawn after 3...c5 4.c3 and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Compensation is unclear and the line is rarely played by strong players.

structure.notes: The centre pawn trade leaves White with only f-pawn and c-pawn against Black's c5.

approach.notes: A rare Bird gambit; chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Tactical but dubious, so not Beginner.
